content: Calorad is a liquid protein supplement designed for weight loss, first introduced to the U.S. and Canadian markets in 1984. It has been marketed through television and radio advertisements. The product is primarily composed of 3,000 mg (3 grams) of Type II hydrolyzed collagen (collagen hydrolysate) derived from either bovine (beef) or marine (tuna) sources, along with 8 mg of aloe vera. These two components are listed as the active ingredients. The supplement is labeled as fat-free and carbohydrate-free, with one serving (1/2 ounce) providing 3 grams of protein and 10 calories. A kosher formulation is also available. The primary claim associated with Calorad is that regular use can lead to weight loss without a reduction in lean muscle mass. The product instructions recommend avoiding food consumption within three hours before sleep, which can contribute to weight loss and body fat reduction. However, most individuals following this regimen alone do not achieve long-term weight loss success. The manufacturer does not claim that Calorad treats or cures diseases but references published clinical trials on Type II hydrolyzed collagen, the main ingredient, in conditions such as osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis, autoimmune diseases, and fibromyalgia. These studies suggest potential benefits of collagen hydrolysate in managing symptoms of these conditions. The manufacturer claims that 40% of users will lose weight within one month, 75% after two months, and 87% after three months. A 30-day satisfaction guarantee is offered, as stated on the manufacturer’s website. To support these claims, Essentially Yours Industries cites a clinical study conducted by Dr. Joel B. Lao, a physician specializing in internal medicine in the Philippines. This unpublished and non-peer-reviewed study involved 50 overweight or obese individuals over a 90-day period. Each participant received one bottle of Calorad per month for three months. By the end of the study, participants experienced an average weight loss of 10 pounds and a reduction of 3 inches in waist circumference, while maintaining lean muscle mass. Notably, 36% of participants gained lean muscle mass during the study. The manufacturer emphasizes that most weight loss regimens result in the loss of lean muscle mass along with fat and water weight, making the preservation of lean muscle mass a unique benefit of Calorad. The rationale for using collagen for weight loss is supported by a precedent in the U.S. patent database, which includes a 30-year-old patent (U.S. Patent 4,042,687) describing the use of predigested protein compositions for treating obesity. This patent outlines the scientific basis for using liquid collagen in weight loss and highlights the importance of not relying on collagen as the sole source of nutrition, a caution also noted on Calorad’s label. When Calorad was first introduced, the manufacturer claimed it could help users lose weight while you sleep, repair joints, and alleviate arthritis symptoms. However, these claims were later removed because they are classified as medical treatment claims, which require FDA approval and substantiation through large-scale clinical trials similar to those conducted by pharmaceutical companies. Essentially Yours Industries has not conducted such rigorous trials for Calorad. The current claims focus on promoting sleep and improving the health and appearance of hair, nails, and skin, which are not considered medical treatment claims. Calorad has not been evaluated by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). All marketing materials for the product include a disclaimer stating that it is a food supplement and is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.
